title: Prompt instrumentation & labeling protocol (draft)
content:
Context and motivation:
- We need a consistent, low-latency way to capture prompts (and minimal context) plus model responses for labeling and quality monitoring without blowing token costs or PII exposure.
- This doc is a personal draft of an ingestion + labeling protocol we can iterate into a product/telemetry spec.
- Priorities: privacy by default, small payloads, robust sampling, ability to link to eval sets and reruns.

Goals:
1) Define an event shape for prompt+response capture usable at both client and gateway.
2) Provide a lightweight schema for downstream labelers and automated metrics.
3) Specify sampling controls, anonymization knobs, and retention tags.
4) Draft an ingestion API and a local buffering/backpressure model for edge SDKs.

Event schema (informal):
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp_utc: iso8601
- request_context: {"model": "name", "route": "api route", "region": "us-west-2"}  <-- in implementation keep as flat k/v string pairs
- prompt_fingerprint: sha256(prefix-limited-prompt)  // used to dedupe and link prompts without storing full prompt
- prompt_preview: first_n_tokens OR heuristic redacted text (see privacy section)
- response_preview: first_n_tokens or deterministic hash + small excerpt
- metadata_tags: ["canary","user-report"]
- sampling_reason: ["global-1pct","error-sample","manual-collection"]
- human_label_id: optional link to label artifact (if labeled)

Sketch: JSON ingestion example (client -> telemetry gateway):
{
  "event_id": "a1b2c3-...",
  "ts": "2025-09-14T18:02:23Z",
  "model": "gpt-4o-redwood-v1",
  "route": "/v1/chat/completions",
  "pfp": "sha256:abcd...",
  "prompt_preview": "[redacted] — user asked: summarize quarterly...",
  "resp_preview": "The quarter saw revenue up 4%...",
  "sample": "error-sample",
  "anonymized": "true"
}

Privacy / PII handling (principles):
- Default: strip all clearly identifiable tokens from prompt_preview using regex heuristics (emails, phone numbers, account ids).
- Prefer fingerprinting+preview over storing full prompt. Full prompt storage allowed only with explicit user consent and separate retention policy.
- Provide a reversible tokenization option for enterprise customers with HSM-backed keys (private-deployments only).
- Maintain a provenance flag: how the text was processed (redacted/hashed/plain).

Sampling strategies (draft):
- Global uniform sample: 0.1% of requests, tunable by customer.
- Error-triggered: sample any request with server error (5xx) or model fallback.
- Quality heuristics: sample responses with length > X tokens or with high perplexity divergence vs baseline.
- Manual capture: product engineers can request 1k session capture for a user by ID (audited).

Labeling taxonomy (minimal):
- label_schema_v1: ["helpful","not_helpful","toxic","hallucination","policy_violation","formatting_issue"]
- label meta: {"annotator_id", "confidence_score", "notes"}  // store as flat strings in ingestion path to avoid nested objects

Backpressure and edge buffering model:
- Clients buffer up to N events (N default 200) in local encrypted ring buffer.
- When buffer full, oldest non-sample events are dropped first.
- Exponential backoff when gateway returns 429/503.
- If persistent failure > 24h and events contain explicit consented full prompts, wipe local buffer to reduce risk.

Ingestion API (HTTP sketch):
POST /v1/telemetry/events
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <telemetry-key>, X-Client-Version
Body: newline-delimited JSON events (ndjson) — each line matches event schema above.
Response: 202 Accepted with body {"ingested": n, "dropped": m, "diagnostic_id": "..."}

Downstream processing ideas:
- Expand fingerprints into clusters for prompt-set evaluations.
- Join with route/cost telemetry to compute per-prompt cost and latency.
- Auto-prioritize events for labeling by a scoring function: severity * user-impact * recency.

Open questions / TODOs (personal):
- Decide default preview token count (16? 32?) and measure re-identification risk.
- Flesh out regex rules vs ML PII scrubber tradeoffs.
- Where to store label artifacts for private deployments — separate S3 with lifecycle?
- Need a small PoC: instrument local SDK with 1% sampling + error sampling, run for 2 weeks on internal beta.
- Discuss legal/Privacy with compliance — especially around EU customers + retention windows.

Notes to self and friction points:
- Keep payloads tiny — NDJSON approach avoids JSON array parsing and is forward-compatible.
- Make SDK opt-out per default for privacy-first developer experience; enterprise can opt-in to full capture.
- Align event "pfp" fingerprint format with other projects (use sha256 + salt per-tenant).

References and breadcrumbs:
- Past doc: CONFLUENCE-1234 (event telemetry primer)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/52 (initial ndjson handler)
- Related tickets: JIRA-LLM-881, JIRA-SEC-210

Quick rollout plan (alpha):
1) Implement client-side NDJSON writer + ring-buffer (2 weeks).
2) Gate: telemetry ingestion endpoint (server) + light validation (1 week).
3) Internal beta with 5 eng teams, 2-weeks (2 weeks).
4) Measure PII leaks, token counts, cost (1 week).

If we decide this approach is viable, next step is to convert this scratchpad into a full spec for the telemetry/instruments repo and schedule a sync with Privacy/Legal and Product Manager.

End of draft — rough and messy, but captures the shape.
